title: Kampi Foldaway Camp Fan
description: Two things go wrong with camping fans. The cheap ones are noisy and run flat by 22:00. The good ones are the size of a suitcase and never come out of the garage. The Kampi Foldaway Camp Fan was picked to solve both: it collapses into its own base, it runs off a battery you top up from any USB-C port, and on the low setting it is quiet enough to sleep next to. It is just as useful at home. When the power goes, the fan does not – and it charges back up from the same power bank you use for your phone. Table height, or floor height The telescopic column runs from 40cm folded to 105cm extended, and locks anywhere in between. On the camp table it points at your face across a game of cards; on the ground next to a stretcher it moves air over the whole tent. The head tilts through 200 degrees , so you can also aim it straight up at a rooftop tent. Four speeds, from a whisper up Five blades and four wind settings – breeze, soft, strong and natural – with 65 degree oscillation to spread the air rather than blast one person. The low setting runs from 12 dB , which is below the sound of your own breathing, and there is a 4-hour timer so it does not run all night if you drop off. The remote is in the box, so you are not climbing out of the sleeping bag to change speed. Charges off anything with USB-C Power bank, laptop, wall plug, or the inverter on the caravan’s dual battery – if it has a USB-C port, it charges this fan. A full charge takes 4 to 6 hours and the 1.5m USB-C cable is included. It will also run while it is plugged in. Folds into its own base The head drops, the column collapses and the whole thing becomes a 22cm x 10.5cm disc. That is a caravan cupboard, a drawer, the gap behind the seat, or the top of the ammo box – not a boot full of fan. Specifications Height 40cm folded, up to 105cm extended Folded size 22cm across x 10.5cm high Fan head 5 blades Speeds 4 (breeze, soft, strong, natural) Noise From 12 dB on the low setting Oscillation 65 degrees side to side Tilt 200 degrees Timer 4 hours Remote Included Power Built-in rechargeable battery, USB-C Charge time 4 to 6 hours to full Colours Black or Pure White In the box Foldaway fan Remote control 1.5m USB-C charging cable A wall charger, power bank or laptop is not included – use the one you already have. title: Vehicle First Aid Kit – Built by First Responders
description: The little brother of our Campsite First Aid Kit , built by the same working first responders at The First Responders . This one is sized for the vehicle: a flat fold-out pouch for the cubbyhole, the door pocket or behind the seat of the bakkie. Burn cover, real wound care and gloves for the roadside moments, and for handing through the window when someone else needs help. What’s inside Item Qty What it’s for Burn dressing 10x10cm (Burn Eaz) 1 Braai, gas and boiling-water burns – cools and covers First aid dressing No. 3 (FAD) 2 Sterile trauma dressing for serious bleeding Sterile gauze 1 Cleaning and covering wounds Plasters 10 The everyday cuts and blisters Crepe bandages 3 Sprains, strains, holding dressings in place Conforming bandages 3 Wraps around joints and awkward spots Triangular bandage 1 Arm sling, splint ties, head wounds Rescue blanket 1 Shock, cold, keeping someone warm until help arrives Nitrile gloves 4 Protect yourself and the patient – put these on first CPR mouthpiece 1 Barrier for rescue breaths Alcohol swabs 10 Cleaning tweezers, scissors and skin around a wound Plastic tape 2 Securing dressings Scissors 1 Cutting bandages – or clothing, when it matters Tweezers 1 Splinters, thorns, ticks The fold-out design opens flat with see-through pockets on both sides, so you can see everything at once instead of digging. A printed contents list is packed inside for restocking after use. Vehicle kit or campsite kit? This kit is built for the vehicle: one of everything, flat enough for the cubbyhole. Camping with kids, a group, or heading somewhere remote? The Campsite First Aid Kit carries more of everything, adds 100ml burn gel, a second rescue blanket, a box of 50 plasters and a proper carry bag with space for your own medicine. Plenty of Kampi hosts and renters keep one of each: this one in the cab, the big one in the camper. title: Lesotho Cross-Border Sticker Kit
description: Sani Pass, Katse Dam or the Roof of Africa? Lesotho is a light-touch crossing with minimal vehicle-marking rules, but the mountain passes mean your papers and a roadworthy rig matter. The Kampi Lesotho cross-border kit keeps it simple: the ZA country oval and a clear guide. What is in the kit ZA country identifier oval for the rear of the rearmost vehicle. Printed fitment and placement guide. Where the sticker goes ZA oval: rear, right-hand side, at least 150 mm clear of the number plate . When towing, fit it to the caravan or trailer. Lesotho asks for no reflective-tape or T-sign . There is a small toll (around R30) at the border. Note that South African travellers may not bring alcohol into Lesotho. How to fit your stickers Clean and dry the panel with soapy water, then wipe with a little methylated spirits so the adhesive grips. Fit in mild shade, not full Kalahari sun : the vinyl sits flatter and the glue cures better between 15°C and 25°C. Peel slowly, lay one edge down first, then smooth from the centre outwards with a cloth or squeegee to push out air bubbles. Press the reflective tape and ovals down hard for 30 seconds and leave them 24 hours before a wash or a long highway run. Worth keeping in the vehicle Reflective warning triangles: carry two, or four when towing. The passes are steep and a breakdown marker matters here. Your vehicle licence, registration papers and a letter of authority for a hired or financed vehicle. Please read before you travel Border requirements change without notice and enforcement differs from one post and one official to the next. This kit and guide are put together in good faith from current travel sources, but they are guidance, not legal advice . Confirm the rules for your route with the relevant roads authority or your border post before you leave, and carry your vehicle licence, registration papers and a police clearance where required.
description_html:
Sani Pass, Katse Dam or the Roof of Africa? Lesotho is a light-touch crossing with minimal vehicle-marking rules, but the mountain passes mean your papers and a roadworthy rig matter. The Kampi Lesotho cross-border kit keeps it simple: the ZA country oval and a clear guide.

What is in the kit

  • ZA country identifier oval for the rear of the rearmost vehicle.
  • Printed fitment and placement guide.

Where the sticker goes

  • ZA oval: rear, right-hand side, at least 150 mm clear of the number plate. When towing, fit it to the caravan or trailer.

Lesotho asks for no reflective-tape or T-sign. There is a small toll (around R30) at the border. Note that South African travellers may not bring alcohol into Lesotho.

How to fit your stickers

  1. Clean and dry the panel with soapy water, then wipe with a little methylated spirits so the adhesive grips.
  2. Fit in mild shade, not full Kalahari sun: the vinyl sits flatter and the glue cures better between 15°C and 25°C.
  3. Peel slowly, lay one edge down first, then smooth from the centre outwards with a cloth or squeegee to push out air bubbles.
  4. Press the reflective tape and ovals down hard for 30 seconds and leave them 24 hours before a wash or a long highway run.

Worth keeping in the vehicle

  • Reflective warning triangles: carry two, or four when towing. The passes are steep and a breakdown marker matters here.
